title: Coefficient ring map from a homogeneous section-ring localization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $S$ its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], $d>0$, $s\in S_d$, and $U\subseteq X$ open. Assume that $s|_U$ is a free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator] of $L^{\otimes d}$ on $U$. There is a unital ring map $\rho:S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ such that for all $n\geq0$ and $\xi\in S_{nd}$, $\rho(\xi/s^n)(s^n)|_U=\xi|_U$.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: Tensoring the assumed free generator gives a free generator of every power L^{tensor nd}; the identification with the degree nd component uses the section ring tensor multiplication. For n=0 this is the tensor unit. Define the coefficient of a degree nd numerator to be its unique scalar in the basis s^n.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: If a/s^n=b/s^m in the homogeneous localization, some k satisfies s^k(a s^m-b s^n)=0. On U the coefficient of this equality relative to s^{k+n+m} is coeff(a)-coeff(b)=0, proving well-definedness. Addition with denominator s^{n+m} adds coefficients, multiplication multiplies coefficients, and 1/1 has coefficient 1. These equations define the unital ring map and give its numerator formula. On the empty open all section types are singletons.
